Automated reporting service for commercial cleaning companies
Owner-operated cleaning companies with 10–30 sites waste hours every week chasing missing photos, following up on incomplete checklists, and assembling client reports. The cleaning happens. The records sit in CrewProof or Janitorial Manager. But someone still has to review everything, hunt down gaps, and package it all into something clients want to see. That someone is usually the owner, grinding through admin at 9 PM instead of growing the business. Ninepm handles the followup and reporting while you keep using your existing software. Nothing changes in your workflow. You keep running jobs the way you always have. We review completion records daily, chase supervisors when something's missing, and send polished monthly updates to your clients. You get back 10+ hours per week and your clients get consistent, professional updates without you lifting a finger. Start with a paid two-week pilot covering five sites at $497. We review records daily, follow up with your team when gaps appear, and deliver a sample client report. If it works, you move to a monthly retainer at $75–$150 per active site depending on how much follow-up your crews need. We cap review frequency and follow-up volume upfront so pricing stays predictable. At $100 per site per month and 250 active sites, this hits $300K ARR. You grow by posting before-and-after report samples in cleaning owner Facebook groups, partnering with software vendors who want their customers to get more value, and earning referrals from ops managers who finally have their nights back. The wedge is simple: we don't replace systems or add complexity. We just do the boring work cleaning companies hate but clients demand. Start manually with one person handling 50–100 sites. Automate the review logic as patterns emerge, but keep human follow-up because supervisors ignore bots. This works as a service first, product later if ever.

Software for brands to put their convention pop-ups on one map and see who shows up
Major conventions scatter valuable brand activations across the city, and nobody knows where to find them. Pop-ups, creator appearances, exclusive merchandise drops, after-parties, restaurant collabs — they all live in different corners of social media, ticketing pages, and group chats. Attendees waste time hunting. Brands waste money on activations nobody discovers. FanMap fixes both problems with a mobile-web map that combines official programming with everything happening off-site. No app download required. Just open the link and see the whole event city at once. You charge brands $500–$2,000 for promoted pins that get verified placement and tracked engagement. Agencies can subscribe at $99–$299/month to build maps for multiple events, run sponsored quests, and access analytics dashboards. White-label editions for organizers get custom pricing. You also earn affiliate revenue from ticket and reservation referrals. Pricing scales with event size and sponsor budgets, but the key is starting small: pick one dense convention like Comic-Con or SXSW, manually curate the map, pre-sell a handful of promoted listings, and prove the model before scaling. The wedge is editorial curation that official apps can't match. You're not just listing venues, you're publishing a useful guide that includes the unofficial stuff attendees actually care about: where the exclusive merch drops are, which bars have viewing parties, when creators are doing meetups.
